condition.label: Kidney transplant — maintenance immunosuppression (tacrolimus, twice daily)
condition.plain_english: Her new kidney only keeps working while she takes the anti-rejection medicine exactly on time, every day, for life.

schedule.conditions: Same two times every day, twelve hours apart.

prompts.en: Did she take the anti-rejection tablet just now?
prompts.zh-Hant: 剛才有冇食咗抗排斥藥？

schedule.event: She is sick (vomits) within an hour of a tablet.

prompts.en: Did she bring the tablet back up?
prompts.zh-Hant: 食完藥之後有冇嘔返出嚟？

prompts.en: What is her temperature this morning?

schedule.event: Any new medicine, supplement or herbal remedy, from any doctor or shop.

prompts.en: Has anyone given her a new medicine, supplement or herbal remedy?
prompts.zh-Hant: 有冇人畀咗新藥、補充劑或者中藥佢食？

schedule.conditions: Laboratory trough level, entered from the clinic result.

rules.why: A single missed dose is the start of the pattern that ends in graft loss, and it is the only point at which it is still trivial to correct.

Undetectable drug levels were present in 53 percent of patients who lost their graft against 13 percent of those who did not, and the first undetectable level came a median of about three years before the loss.
A tablet that was brought back up was never delivered, and nobody can tell from the pill box that this happened.
Immunosuppression removes the usual signs of infection, so a fever is treated as significant until the transplant team says otherwise.
Ordinary medicines, supplements and some foods change how much anti-rejection drug reaches the blood, and the person prescribing them usually does not know she is a transplant patient.
Swinging drug levels are themselves a validated warning sign, independently of whether any single level looks acceptable.
No answer is not the same as nothing wrong, and it is the most common way a monitoring routine fails quietly.

message.ask: Add this to her file for the next clinic visit.
message.because: A pattern has appeared that is worth seeing alongside her bloods.
message.if_ignored: Nothing happens today, but the pattern will not be visible at the appointment.

message.ask: Please check with her that the tablet was actually taken, and tell us what you find.
message.because: One dose was recorded as missed, or nobody has answered for longer than expected.
message.if_ignored: Single misses turn into a habit, and the habit is what costs the kidney.

message.ask: Please contact the transplant team today.
message.because: Something has happened that changes how much anti-rejection medicine is reaching her blood.
message.if_ignored: Rejection begins silently, and by the time it is felt the damage is usually permanent.

message.ask: Telephone the transplant unit now — do not wait for the next clinic.
message.because: She has a fever while on medicine that hides infection, or a same-day contact went unanswered.
message.if_ignored: Infection in a transplant patient can move from mild to dangerous within a day.

message.ask: Take her to the emergency department, or call an ambulance.
message.because: An urgent contact has gone unanswered and she may be developing an infection she cannot fight.
message.if_ignored: This is the point at which delay becomes life-threatening.

prohibitions: Never tell anyone to change, skip, double or make up a dose. Missed-dose handling belongs to the transplant centre's own protocol.
Never state or imply that rejection is occurring. The agent reports observations and routes them; it does not diagnose.
Never reassure. If a rule did not fire, say nothing rather than saying everything is fine.
Never send clinical detail to a role whose may_receive list does not include clinical_detail.

sources.citation: Tacrolimus intrapatient variability and rejection are associated with inferior allograft outcomes after kidney transplantation, Frontiers in Nephrology, 2025.
Local transplant centre maintenance immunosuppression protocol — SYNTHETIC PLACEHOLDER for demonstration. A real plan carries the issuing unit's own document.

outcome_metrics: doses taken on time per month
days between a missed dose and a human acknowledging it
